problems.title: A rational inequality with odd-power factors
problems.question: Solve $[(x-2x^2)^3(3x+9)]/(-x^2+5x-6)\le0$.
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
formulas: Factor numerator as $3x^3(1-2x)^3(x+3)$ and denominator as −(x−2)(x−3).
steps: Critical points are −3,0,1/2,2,3. Numerator zeros are included; poles 2,3 are excluded.
The signs in consecutive intervals from left to right are −,+,−,+,−,+. Keep the negative intervals and zeros.

problems.title: An area-product identity for intersecting diagonals
problems.question: In convex ABCD, diagonals meet at O. Prove S(AOB)S(COD)=S(BOC)S(AOD).
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
formulas: Triangle area with included angle is ab sin theta/2; supplementary angles have equal sine.
steps: Writing all four areas gives respectively AO·BO·s/2, CO·DO·s/2, BO·CO·s/2, AO·DO·s/2, where s is the common positive sine.
Both products equal AO·BO·CO·DO·s²/4, proving the identity.
problems.answer: The two area products are equal.

problems.question: For which a is the vertex of y=(x−2a)²−3a+1 in quadrant II?
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
steps: Require 2a<0 and 1−3a>0. The first gives a<0 and already guarantees the second.

problems.title: A trapezoid’s midline divides its area
problems.question: A diagonal divides a trapezoid’s area in ratio 3:5. In what ratio does its midline divide the area?
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
formulas: The diagonal-triangle area ratio equals the base ratio. The midline length is the base mean.
steps: Let the bases be 3t,5t and height h. The midline is 4t and each smaller trapezoid has height h/2.
Their areas are (3t+4t)h/4 and (4t+5t)h/4, in ratio 7:9.

problems.title: Distance sums on a number line
problems.question: Solve (a) |x−3|+|x+2|=5; (b) |x−1|+|x−8|>9.
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
formulas: Between two endpoints, the sum of distances is their separation; outside, it grows linearly.
steps: (a) The endpoint distance is 5. Equality holds exactly for x between −2 and 3, including endpoints.
(b) Between 1 and 8 the sum is 7. On the left it is 9−2x>9 iff x<0; on the right it is 2x−9>9 iff x>9.

problems.title: Shaded triangles in four equal-height strips
problems.question: The source triangle side is divided into four equal parts with parallel cross-sections and diagonal strip cuts as drawn. Find shaded:unshaded area.
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
formulas: Cross-section lengths grow linearly with distance from the top; a triangle area is base×height/2.
steps: Use total triangle area as 16 units. Each strip has height one quarter of the full altitude. The shaded triangles have bases 1/4,2/4,3/4,4/4 of the full base.
Their areas are 1,2,3,4 units, totaling 10. The unshaded area is 16−10=6.
The ratio is 10:6=5:3.

problems.title: A root expression with a real-root restriction
problems.question: x₁,x₂ solve x²+2ax−7a=0. Minimize x₁²+x₂²+x₁x₂ for real roots.
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
formulas: Vieta gives E=(x₁+x₂)²−x₁x₂=4a²+7a. Real roots require a(a+7)≥0.
steps: The allowed parameters are a≤−7 or a≥0. On a≥0, E≥0 with equality at a=0. On a≤−7, E≥147.
Therefore the minimum is zero, at the double root x₁=x₂=0.
Completing the square without the real-root restriction would give −49/16 at a=−7/8, but that equation has nonreal roots.
problems.note: The unconstrained algebraic minimum −49/16 is invalid if the equation’s solutions are required to be real. With complex roots allowed it would be the formal alternative.

problems.title: A corrected letter changes a zero-area triangle
problems.question: AD:DB=2:1, BE:EC=1:3 and AE intersects DC at K. The source corrects the requested triangle from AKE to AKC. Find the corrected area ratio to ABC.
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
formulas: Balanced masses can be assigned A=3,B=6,C=2; barycentric height ratios give area ratios with a shared base.
steps: D has mass 9 and E has mass 8. At the intersection K, the vertex masses are proportional to 3:6:2.
Thus K’s altitude above AC is 6/(3+6+2)=6/11 of B’s altitude. Triangles AKC and ABC share base AC, giving ratio 6/11.
If the uncorrected letters AKE are read literally, A,K,E are collinear and that area ratio is 0.
problems.note: The printed text and extracted text show AKE, with a visible red correction to C in the source. Both readings are explained explicitly.

problems.title: Two requested root intervals are impossible
problems.question: Find a for which ax²+(2a−1)x+a+1=0 has one root in (−1,0) and another in (0,1).
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
formulas: For a genuine quadratic, outside its two roots its sign is the sign of a.
steps: At x=−1 the polynomial is always 2>0. Since −1 lies left of both requested roots, this forces a>0.
At x=0, between those roots, its sign would then have to be negative. But its value is a+1>0, a contradiction.
a=0 gives a linear equation and cannot have two roots.
